SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SINGING GAMES
Subject: MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Singing games helps you succeed in MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: SINGING GAMES
Study Singing games like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.

If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Observe game etiquette for singing games to be done in pairs own and others respect, and in groups to encourage team

What this means
In this part you learn to observe game etiquette for singing games to be done in pairs own and others respect, and in groups to encourage team. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: observe game etiquette for singing games to be done in pairs own and others respect, and in groups to encourage team.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Singing games” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can observe game etiquette for singing games to be done in pairs own and others respect, and in groups to encourage team. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Share available resources work and responsibility during performance of •

What this means
In this part you learn to share available resources work and responsibility during performance of •. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: share available resources work and responsibility during performance of •.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Singing games in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can share available resources work and responsibility during performance of •. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Singing games is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Singing games” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: observe game etiquette for singing games to be done in pairs own and others respect, and in groups to encourage team)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Singing games in your own words. (skill: share available resources work and responsibility during performance of •)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Singing games to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: observe game etiquette for singing games to be done in pairs own and others respect, and in groups to encourage team.
3. Practise this skill: share available resources work and responsibility during performance of •.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Singing games from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Singing games: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Singing games?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Singing games means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: observe game etiquette for singing games to be done in pairs own and others respect, and in groups to encourage team.
5. Be able to: share available resources work and responsibility during performance of •.
